To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

consumers and their case managers do not agree on how much help is needed or received with most mental health and community service needs, and consumers rely on nonmental health system sources for help with most community service needs.

consumers with serious and persistent psychiatric disorders perceive that the majority of their mental health and community supports needs are not being met, whereas their case managers perceive that the majority are being met.
Consumers with SPMI and their case managers had different perceptions of help needed and received for mental health and community supports.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model for the assessment of service needs that is based on the perceptions of both consumers and their case managers.
the development and testing of an instrument to identify consumers' and case manager's perceptions of help needed and received.
the extent to which consumers' and case mangers' ratings of service needs are congruent, as well as the sources of help that consumers identify.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this research suggest that consumers' and case mangers' perceptions of help needed and received differ.
the results of this study indicate that consumers' and case manager's perceptions of help needed are not in agreement.
the findings are inconclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers and their case managers do not agree on the amount of help consumers receive for their needs.
we need to better understand what is needed and how to best meet those needs.

the consumers' needs for community supports are not being adequately met, and that the mental health system needs to do a much better job of providing information and assistance to consumers to help them access community supports.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumers' and case manager perceptions of help needed and received with mental health services and community support services do not always match.
the consumer perspective is critical to understanding the needs of consumers with serious mental illness.
consumers' perceptions of help needed and received with mental health services should be included in the evaluation process.
